programs.name: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)
programs.duration: 5 years, 180 days per entry, extendable once to ~360 days continuous
programs.cost: 10,000 THB (~$275) application fee + 1,900 THB per extension
programs.tax: Territorial — foreign income generally untaxed if remitted rules met
programs.note: Renewal/extension terms are now confirmed and stable. But enforcement has tightened since 2024: funds must sit in your account 3+ months before applying, language schools were excluded from the soft-power category, and rejection rates have climbed through 2025-2026 — still the most flexible entry point in the region, just less forgiving on paperwork than at launch.

programs.name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass
programs.tax: 0% tax on foreign-sourced income — carve-out currently runs 2022–2026, confirm current status before long-term planning
programs.note: Most predictable paperwork in the region — but 'tech work' is interpreted narrowly, generalist freelancers sometimes declined. Worth double-checking whether the tax exemption has been renewed past 2026 before committing multi-year plans here.

programs.name: Second Home Visa (Bali route)
programs.tax: Complex — consult a local tax advisor before staying past 183 days
programs.note: High capital bar but by far the longest runway. The lower-threshold E33G remote-worker route ($60k/yr income, 1-year permit, now confirmed renewable online indefinitely) is a well-established alternative. Important: Bali immigration launched a 100-officer enforcement task force in April 2026 actively patrolling for people working on tourist visas — hundreds have been deported in 2025-2026. Don't work remotely from Indonesia without a proper permit.

programs.name: Digital Nomad Visa
programs.duration: 6 months, not renewable — but you can reapply after a 6-month cooling-off period outside Japan
programs.tax: Short-stay, generally outside local tax residency
programs.note: Best for a high-earning short cultural stint, not a long-term base — you'll need to leave and wait 6 months before reapplying, so it works better as a recurring 6-months-on/6-months-off pattern than most people expect.

programs.name: 90-day e-visa (workaround)
programs.tax: Undefined for remote workers — legal gray area
programs.note: No dedicated nomad visa exists, and none has materialized despite a proposed 10-year Golden Visa still sitting unenacted as of mid-2026. Widely used anyway, but you're technically on a tourist visa while working — treat as short-term only.

programs.name: Digital Nomad Visa (EO 86)
programs.funds: No separate deposit — income proof required
programs.duration: 1 year, renewable once (up to 2 years total)
programs.tax: Non-tax resident — foreign-sourced income not taxed locally
programs.note: Launched via Executive Order 86 in 2025 and now fully operational — no longer 'in development.' One real catch: it requires your home country to offer Filipinos a reciprocal digital nomad visa, and no official list of qualifying countries has been published yet, so confirm eligibility directly with your nearest Philippine embassy before assuming you qualify.
